question.text: According to the chapter's historical narrative on the growth of alternative investments, the period described as one of 'unprecedented success for the private equity industry' — during which more money was raised, invested and distributed back to investors than in any other period — is:

answer.text: The 1950s-1960s, when modern portfolio theory emerged
The 1980s boom just before the late-1980s setback
The period since 2014 per the Bain Private Equity Report

explanation.text: The Logic: The chapter cites: 'According to the Bain Private Equity Report, the period since 2014 was that of unprecedented success for the private equity industry. During that span, more money was raised, invested and distributed back to investors than in any other period in the industry's history.' The Trap: (A) the 1950s-60s saw MPT's emergence but not unprecedented PE raising. (B) The 1980s boom ended in setbacks. (C) The dotcom era saw losses, not unprecedented distributions. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covers the same historical timeline. Global-market reference papers (McKinsey Global Private Markets, Preqin) are cross-referenced. Manager's Pro-Tip: Cat I/II GPs raising fresh vintages should benchmark against the post-2014 distribution pace in their LP pitchbook, but also reference the 2022-24 slowdown in global PE distributions (DPI compression). A balanced historical context beats a bull-case-only deck in sophisticated LP meetings.
